Soojin / Liam — quick reply from Procurement & Accounting: the fastest acceptable path is:

1) An updated, signed W-9 that reflects the subsidiary legal name and subsidiary EIN (signed by an authorized officer).
2) A bank verification letter on bank letterhead confirming the subsidiary legal name and account ownership (no notarization required).
3) If the signer on the W-9 is not listed as an officer, include a one-page authorized signer attestation on company letterhead (simple template is fine).

If you can upload the three documents to the DocuSign envelope or attach them here, Procurement will proceed to clear the PO and publish the PO number. Once the PO is active, payments will be scheduled to the account in the bank letter on the normal net terms.

Liam — as a small operational ask, please ensure the W-9 filled name exactly matches the bank letter name (matching punctuation and DBA if present). If you expect any delay I can provisionally create the PO with a conditional note, but funds release will not happen until the documents match.
